statement: Build a playable Sudoku game as one static HTML file (HTML, CSS and JavaScript, no build step) that generates unique-solution puzzles in the browser at Easy, Medium and Hard, with pencil notes, undo, hint, check and a timer. The file includes step-by-step steps for deploying it to the user's own Vercel account.
audience: People who want to play Sudoku in a web browser, on desktop or mobile.
standards: Single index.html file with inline CSS and JavaScript; CDN libraries allowed; no build step.
Every generated puzzle has exactly one solution, enforced by a solver inside the file.
No browser storage: no saved games or saved times.
Playable on desktop and mobile screen widths.
Open inputs appear on the site as clearly marked placeholders.
rules: Scope is limited to the CEO's decisions: browser-generated puzzles at three difficulties; pencil notes, undo, hint, check and timer; deploy steps for Vercel.
No outward-facing action, including publishing to Vercel, is taken by the department.
Do not add persistence or features beyond the chosen scope without a new Identity ruling.
done_when: The file is a single HTML document with inline CSS and JavaScript and needs no build step.
The page shows a 9x9 grid and lets the player select a cell and enter or clear a number 1 to 9.
The page has a New Game control with Easy, Medium and Hard options, and puzzles are generated in the browser by code in the file.
The file contains a solver that counts solutions, and the generator only accepts a puzzle when the solver finds exactly one solution.
Entries that duplicate a number in the same row, column or 3x3 box are visibly highlighted.
Pencil-note mode lets the player toggle small candidate numbers in a cell, and entering a number updates or clears that cell's notes consistently.
An Undo control reverses the player's last moves, including note changes, one step at a time.
A Hint control fills one correct cell, and a Check control marks entries that differ from the solution.
A running timer is visible during play and stops when the puzzle is completed.
A completion message appears when the grid is fully and correctly filled.
The file contains no use of localStorage, sessionStorage, cookies or IndexedDB.
The page contains a deployment section with numbered steps for publishing the file to the user's own Vercel account, and a marked placeholder for the live URL.
The layout stays usable at a 360px-wide screen and on a desktop screen.
open_inputs: Live Vercel URL of the deployed game (shown on the site as a marked placeholder until the Requester deploys it).
dropped_from_brief: Publishing the game live on Vercel is not part of the charter. The department makes no outward-facing action and holds no Vercel credentials, so it delivers the single index.html plus deploy steps for the Requester to run. The Requester must agree to this before work starts.
